examples.en: It's the weekend, so the market is really teeming with people.

examples.ko: 냄비 속에서 물이 버글버글 끓고 있어요.
examples.en: The water in the pot is bubbling away.

examples.ko: 방학 때 해수욕장은 늘 사람으로 버글버글해요.
examples.en: During vacation the beach is always packed with people.
The morning subway is jam-packed with people, so it's hard.
I can hear the soybean stew bubbling.
On the festival day the square was swarming with people.

explain: 사람이 아주 많이 모여 빽빽할 때와 물이나 찌개가 끓을 때 둘 다 쓰는 말이에요. '북적북적'과 비슷하지만 버글버글은 끓는 모습에도 쓸 수 있어요. '버글버글하다'로도 자주 말해요.
explain_en: It is used both when a place is crowded with people and when water or stew is bubbling. It is similar to '북적북적', but 버글버글 can also describe boiling. You can also say '버글버글하다'.

examples.ko: 아기가 안기기 싫은지 한참 버둥거리다가 울었어요.
examples.en: The baby squirmed for a while, as if not wanting to be held, and then cried.
The puppy that fell into the water flailed desperately.
Please don't kick your legs around while sitting on the chair.
The bug is flipped over and flailing its legs.

examples.ko: 혼자 버둥거려 봐도 문제가 해결되지 않아요.
examples.en: Even if I struggle on my own, the problem doesn't get solved.

examples.ko: 아이가 장난감을 사 달라며 바닥에서 버둥거려요.
examples.en: The child is thrashing on the floor, asking me to buy a toy.

explain: 팔다리를 크게 휘저으며 몸부림칠 때 쓰고, 어려운 상황에서 벗어나려고 애쓰는 모습에도 비유로 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '버둥대다'도 말해요. '발버둥을 치다'와 이어서 기억하면 쉬워요.
explain_en: It describes flailing your arms and legs, and also figuratively trying hard to get out of a difficult situation. '버둥대다' means the same. It helps to link it with '발버둥을 치다'.

examples.en: The baby is laughing, kicking its legs about.
The caught fish is thrashing around in my hand.

examples.ko: 아이가 안아 달라고 버둥버둥 몸을 비틀어요.
examples.en: The child twists and squirms, asking to be picked up.

examples.ko: 바닥에 뒤집힌 거북이가 버둥버둥 애쓰고 있어요.
examples.en: The turtle flipped over on the floor is struggling hard.

examples.ko: 고양이가 목욕이 싫어서 버둥버둥 난리를 쳐요.
examples.en: The cat hates baths and makes a big fuss, thrashing about.

examples.ko: 버둥버둥 애를 써 봐도 일이 풀리지 않아요.
examples.en: No matter how hard I struggle, things don't work out.

explain: 팔다리를 크게 흔들며 움직이는 모양이에요. '바둥바둥'은 더 작고 가벼운 느낌이에요. 어려운 일 앞에서 애쓰는 모습을 말할 때도 써요.
explain_en: It shows the motion of waving arms and legs about widely. '바둥바둥' feels smaller and lighter. It can also describe struggling hard against a difficult situation.

examples.en: The willow branches sway gently in the spring breeze.
Willow branches hang long by the stream.
My grandmother made a basket out of willow branches.
Buds have started to sprout on the willow branches.

examples.ko: 연못 옆 버들가지 아래에서 잠깐 쉬었어요.
examples.en: I rested for a while under the willow branches by the pond.

examples.ko: 이 오래된 노래에는 버들가지 이야기가 나와요.
examples.en: This old song mentions willow branches.

explain: 버드나무의 가늘고 긴 가지예요. 아래로 늘어진 모습 때문에 봄 풍경을 말할 때 자주 나와요. '버들'은 버드나무를 뜻하는 말로, '버들잎'처럼 다른 말과도 붙어요.
explain_en: These are the thin, long branches of a willow tree. Because they hang down gracefully, they often appear when describing spring scenery. '버들' refers to the willow tree and also combines with other words, as in '버들잎'.

examples.en: When spring comes, pussy willows bloom by the brook.
When I touched the pussy willow, it was soft like down.
The children played holding pussy willow twigs they had snapped off.
The fluffy pussy willow is really cute.

examples.ko: 이른 봄에 버들강아지를 보면 기분이 좋아져요.
examples.en: Seeing pussy willows in early spring makes me feel good.
The pussy willow in the photo sparkles in the sunlight.

explain: 진짜 강아지가 아니라 이른 봄에 버드나무 종류에 피는 솜털 같은 꽃이삭이에요. 봄이 오는 것을 알리는 모습으로 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: Despite the name, it is not a puppy but the fuzzy, downy flower spike that appears on willow trees in early spring. It fits well when talking about the arrival of spring.

examples.ko: 버르장머리 없이 어른께 말하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not talk to elders so rudely.
That child has no manners at all.

examples.ko: 자꾸 그러면 그 버르장머리를 고쳐 줄 거예요.
examples.en: If you keep doing that, I'll straighten out that bad attitude of yours.
Who taught you such bad manners?

examples.ko: 어릴 때 버르장머리를 잘 잡아 줘야 해요.
examples.en: You have to set good manners right when they are young.

examples.ko: 저 버르장머리 좀 보세요, 인사도 안 하네요.
examples.en: Look at that attitude, he doesn't even say hello.

explain: '버릇'보다 거칠고 속된 말이라서 예의 없는 태도를 나무랄 때 많이 써요. '버르장머리가 없다', '버르장머리를 고치다'처럼 말해요. 어른이 아랫사람에게 하는 말이라 윗사람에게 쓰면 무례해요.
explain_en: It is a rougher, more colloquial word than '버릇', mostly used to scold rude behavior. You say '버르장머리가 없다' or '버르장머리를 고치다'. It is spoken by elders to younger people, so using it toward a superior is rude.

examples.ko: 발표 때 긴장해서 말이 자꾸 버벅댔어요.
examples.en: I got nervous during the presentation and kept stumbling over my words.
My computer is old, so programs keep lagging.
I felt frustrated because I kept stumbling when trying to speak English.
I practiced beforehand so I wouldn't stumble in the interview.
The game was lagging, so I couldn't win.

examples.ko: 처음 하는 일이라 좀 버벅대도 괜찮아요.
examples.en: It's your first time doing this, so it's fine if you fumble a bit.

explain: 말이나 동작이 매끄럽지 않고 자꾸 막힐 때 쓰는 구어체예요. 요즘은 컴퓨터나 게임이 끊기고 느려질 때도 많이 말해요. 같은 뜻으로 '버벅거리다'도 써요.
explain_en: This is a colloquial word for when speech or movement keeps getting stuck and isn't smooth. These days it is also used when a computer or game lags. '버벅거리다' means the same.

examples.ko: 마른 낙엽을 밟으니 버석버석 소리가 나요.
examples.en: When I step on dry leaves, they make a crunchy rustling sound.
My hair is damaged, so it feels dry and brittle when I touch it.
It's winter and my hands are dry, so they're getting rough and cracked.

examples.ko: 오래된 마른 종이를 만지면 버석버석 소리가 나요.
examples.en: Touching old, dry paper makes a dry rustling sound.

examples.ko: 마른 짚을 뒤지는 소리가 버석버석 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear someone rustling through dry straw.
He walked through the dry grass with a rustling sound.

explain: 마르고 건조한 것이 스치거나 부서질 때 나는 소리와 느낌이에요. '바삭바삭'은 음식에 쓰지만, 버석버석은 낙엽, 종이, 머리카락처럼 마른 것에 써요. '버석버석한 피부'처럼 푸석푸석한 느낌도 말해요.
explain_en: It describes the sound and feel of dry things rubbing or crumbling. '바삭바삭' is used for crispy food, while 버석버석 is for dry things such as leaves, paper, and hair. It can also describe a dry, rough feel as in '버석버석한 피부'.

examples.ko: 퀴즈 시간에 버저를 먼저 눌러야 해요.
examples.en: In the quiz, you have to press the buzzer first.

examples.ko: 문 앞에 있는 버저를 눌러 주세요.
examples.en: Please press the buzzer at the door.
The buzzer sounded when the exam time ended.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 버저가 울리기 직전에 공을 넣었어요.
examples.en: That player scored just before the buzzer sounded.

examples.ko: 회사 입구 버저가 고장 나서 전화로 연락했어요.
examples.en: The buzzer at the company entrance was broken, so I called by phone.

examples.ko: 버저 소리가 너무 커서 깜짝 놀랐어요.
examples.en: The buzzer sound was so loud that I was startled.

explain: 전기로 '삐-' 하는 소리를 내는 장치예요. 퀴즈 프로그램이나 농구 경기의 종료 신호로 자주 나와요. 집 문 앞에서 사람을 부르는 것은 보통 '초인종'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a device that makes a buzzing 'beep' sound by electricity. It often appears in quiz shows and as the end signal in basketball games. The thing at a home door for calling people is usually called '초인종'.

examples.ko: 그는 버젓한 직장에 다니면서도 불평만 해요.
examples.en: He works at a decent job and yet only complains.
It's a small shop, but the sign looks quite respectable.

examples.ko: 이제 나도 버젓해 보이는 직장인이 됐어요.
examples.en: Now I've become a proper-looking office worker too.

examples.ko: 버젓하지 않은 집이라 손님을 부르기 부끄러워요.
examples.en: It's not a decent house, so I'm embarrassed to invite guests.

examples.ko: 대낮에 버젓이 쓰레기를 버리는 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: Some people dump trash openly in broad daylight.
The once respectable shop suddenly closed down.

explain: 번듯하고 떳떳하다는 뜻으로 '버젓한 직장'처럼 써요. 나쁜 뜻은 부사 '버젓이'에서 나와서, 잘못을 하고도 거리낌 없이 하는 모습을 말해요. '버젓이 거짓말하다'처럼 써요. 좋은 뜻은 '어엿하다', '번듯하다'와 비슷해요.
explain_en: As an adjective it means decent and respectable, as in '버젓한 직장'. The negative sense comes from the adverb '버젓이', which describes doing something wrong without any shame, as in '버젓이 거짓말하다'. The positive sense is close to '어엿하다' and '번듯하다'.

examples.en: The cherries on the cherry tree have ripened to black.

examples.ko: 봄이 지나면 길에 버찌가 많이 떨어져요.
examples.en: After spring passes, many cherries fall on the street.
If you step on cherries, your shoes get stained dark red.
The children picked cherries and put them in their mouths.
Cherry-blossom-tree cherries are much smaller than regular cherries.

examples.ko: 이 버찌로 잼을 만들 수 있을까요?
examples.en: Can we make jam with these cherries?

explain: 벚나무의 열매예요. 체리와 비슷하게 생겼지만, 먹으려고 사는 과일은 보통 '체리'라고 해요. 길가의 벚나무 아래에서 봄이 끝날 무렵에 많이 볼 수 있어요.
explain_en: This is the fruit of the cherry-blossom tree. It looks like a cherry, but the fruit people buy to eat is usually called '체리'. You can often see them under roadside cherry trees around the end of spring.

examples.en: I put up a support post so the tree wouldn't fall over.
My family is my biggest pillar of support.

examples.ko: 그 친구가 힘든 시절 버팀목이 되어 주었어요.
examples.en: That friend was my pillar of support in hard times.

examples.ko: 어려운 때 버팀목이 될 사람이 필요해요.
examples.en: In difficult times, I need someone I can lean on.

examples.ko: 농업은 지역 경제의 버팀목 역할을 해요.
examples.en: Agriculture plays the role of a mainstay of the local economy.

examples.ko: 토마토 줄기에 버팀목을 대 주면 잘 자라요.
examples.en: If you add a stake to the tomato stem, it grows well.

explain: 원래는 쓰러지지 않게 받치는 나무인데, 일상에서는 힘들 때 기대고 의지할 수 있는 사람이나 존재를 비유로 많이 말해요. '버팀목이 되다', '버팀목으로 삼다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It literally means a piece of wood that props something up, but in daily life it is often used figuratively for a person or thing you can lean on in hard times. It appears in phrases like '버팀목이 되다' and '버팀목으로 삼다'.

en: with a scratching sound; with scrape

examples.en: My arm was itchy, so I scratched it hard.

examples.ko: 빨래에 묻은 얼룩을 벅벅 문질러 닦았어요.
examples.en: I scrubbed the stain on the laundry hard to clean it.

examples.ko: 개가 문을 벅벅 긁는 소리가 들려요.
examples.en: I can hear the dog scratching at the door.
The child scrubbed his hair vigorously and came out.
I'm upset because the cat keeps scratching the sofa.

examples.ko: 그는 졸린 얼굴을 손으로 벅벅 비볐어요.
examples.en: He rubbed his sleepy face hard with his hands.

explain: 거칠고 힘주어 긁거나 문지를 때 쓰는 말이에요. '박박'과 비슷하지만 소리가 더 굵게 들려요. 보통 '벅벅 긁다', '벅벅 문지르다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is used for scratching or rubbing roughly and with force. It is similar to '박박' but sounds deeper and heavier. It usually appears as '벅벅 긁다' or '벅벅 문지르다'.

examples.en: I polished my shoes and now they shine glossily.
It only looks slick on the outside, and the inside is not great.
Oil got on my hand and it became greasy and shiny.
He must have put oil on his hair, since it shines glossily.
Be careful of ads that are wrapped up so slickly.
The newly polished floor gleams smoothly.

explain: 기름기나 윤기가 돌아 매끈하게 빛나는 모양이에요. 비유로 겉만 그럴듯하고 속은 비었다는 부정적인 느낌으로도 많이 써요. 보통 '번드르르하다' 모양으로 말해요.

phrases.example: 그 사람은 말만 번드르르해서 믿을 수가 없어요.
phrases.en: He is all talk, so I can't trust him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말은 그럴듯하게 잘하지만 실제 행동이나 실속이 없다고 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to criticize someone who speaks smoothly but has no real action or substance behind the words.

explain_en: It describes a smooth shine from oil or gloss. Figuratively, it often has a negative feel of looking good only on the outside while being empty inside. It is usually used in the form '번드르르하다'.

examples.en: The cat's eyes flashed in the darkness.

examples.ko: 회의 중에 좋은 생각이 번득여서 메모했어요.
examples.en: A good idea flashed into my mind during the meeting, so I took a note.
I can see the window glass flashing in the sunlight.

examples.ko: 그의 눈에서 번득이던 빛이 잊히지 않아요.
examples.en: I can't forget the glint that flashed in his eyes.
Lightning flashed, and soon thunder rolled.

examples.ko: 그 학생은 가끔 번득이는 아이디어를 내요.
examples.en: That student sometimes comes up with brilliant ideas.

explain: 빛이 잠깐 강하게 빛날 때 쓰고, 좋은 생각이 갑자기 떠오를 때도 비유로 써요. '번뜩이다'와 거의 같은 뜻으로 쓰여요. 눈빛이나 아이디어를 말할 때 특히 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is used when light shines strongly for a moment, and figuratively when a good idea suddenly comes to mind. It is used almost the same as '번뜩이다'. It especially appears when describing a look in the eyes or an idea.

examples.en: I ate greasy food and my lips are shiny.
My face was getting oily and shiny, so I fixed my makeup.
The newly painted floor gleams with a glossy shine.
My forehead is shiny because of sweat.
I went to the interview wearing shiny shoes.
He must have put on too much gel, because his hair looked greasy.

explain: 기름기나 물기 때문에 표면이 매끈하고 윤이 날 때 써요. 구두나 바닥에는 중립적이지만, 사람 얼굴이나 머리에는 기름져 보인다는 느낌이 있어요. 빛이 반짝이는 '반짝이다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when a surface looks smooth and shiny because of oil or moisture. It is neutral for shoes or floors, but for a person's face or hair it suggests an oily look. It differs from '반짝이다', which is about sparkling light.

examples.en: Sweat is glistening on his forehead.
After eating chicken, my mouth is all greasy.
The new car shines glossily in the sunlight.
Because of the oil, your face looks shiny.
I polished my shoes until they gleamed and wore them out.

examples.ko: 번들번들한 책상 위에 먼지가 하나도 없어요.
examples.en: There isn't any dust on the glossy desk.

explain: 기름기나 윤기로 표면이 매끈하게 빛나는 모양이에요. 사람 얼굴에 쓰면 기름져 보인다는 느낌이 있어서 칭찬으로는 잘 쓰지 않아요. '번들거리다'와 같은 계열의 말이에요.
explain_en: It shows a surface shining smoothly from oil or gloss. Used for a person's face, it suggests an oily look, so it is not used as a compliment. It belongs to the same family as '번들거리다'.

examples.ko: 그 친구는 번듯한 직장에 다니고 있어요.
examples.en: That friend works at a respectable job.
It's a small house, but it looks quite decent from the outside.
I dressed neatly and went to the interview.
He has a broad forehead and a well-shaped, handsome face.

examples.ko: 번듯한 집 한 채 갖는 게 꿈이에요.
examples.en: My dream is to own a decent house.
Even if it isn't a fancy place, it's fine as long as it's comfortable.

explain: 생김새가 반듯하고 보기 좋을 때, 또 직장이나 집처럼 어디에 내놓아도 부끄럽지 않을 만큼 제대로 갖춰졌을 때 써요. '어엿하다'와 비슷하고, 보통 '번듯한 직장'처럼 말해요. 좋은 뜻으로 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It describes things that look neat and good, and things like a job or house that are properly established enough to be presented anywhere without shame. It is close to '어엿하다' and often appears as '번듯한 직장'. It is a positive word.
